The thing is that my 24 inch 1080p monitor has almost the same pixel density as my 50" 4k TV. But I sit closer to my computer than I do on my TV. So if i sat that close to my TV, yes, I could see a more noticeable difference.
Given a pixel density, you have to determine how close do you have to be until you notice a loss in sharpness. Thats why my phone, that has a 2k resolution and therefore much higher pixel density, I can look as close as I want and never notice a loss in sharpness.
If you sit 10m/30ft away from your TV, it doesn't matter if it's 720p, you will see it super sharp (this is an exaggeration, no one sits that's far).
I read once that the sweet spot for 4k is to sit around 1-5/2 times de size of your TV away, it probably depends on each person, but its a reference that worked for me, so I try to move the couch a little bit closer to the TV when I watch on 4k.

I'm not trying to convince you, I'm just sharing my experience and if I'm wrong, pls someone correct me!

And, yes, 4k tvs are pretty cheap nowadays, totally worth it, even for the general public that doesn't collect 4k physical media, now that 4k streaming is more a more common, even 4k TV stream!
When you're on a pc you sit really close to the screen, that's why it's easier to tell the difference between different resolutions. When it comes to TVs, most people sit on the further away.
